Regresión Poisson Robusta vs Regresión Log Binomial

CFMV

24 de mayo del 2025

A continuación se presentan los modelos de una Regresión Poisson con varianza robusta y de una Regresión Log Binomial.

REGRESIÓN POISSON ROBUSTA

# Librerías

library(sandwich)
library(lmtest)
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(performance)
library(sjPlot)
library(ggeffects)
library(equatiomatic)
library(emmeans)
library(gtsummary)
library(logbin)
library(MASS)

Datos Simulados

# Simular datos
set.seed(123)

n <- 1000

producto <- factor(sample(c("Lácteo", "Cárnico", "Vegetal"), n, replace = TRUE))
proveedor <- factor(sample(c("A", "B"), n, replace = TRUE))
temperatura <- round(rnorm(n, mean = 72, sd = 5), 1)  # temperatura de cocción

# Coeficientes simulados (lacteo base, proveedor A base)
beta0 <- -2.0
beta_prod <- c(Cárnico = 0.6, Vegetal = 0.9)  # efecto sobre RR
beta_provB <- 0.4
beta_temp <- 0.03

# Calcular eta y probabilidad
eta <- beta0 +
  ifelse(producto == "Cárnico", beta_prod["Cárnico"],
         ifelse(producto == "Vegetal", beta_prod["Vegetal"], 0)) +
  ifelse(proveedor == "B", beta_provB, 0) +
  beta_temp * temperatura

p <- exp(eta)  # log link para riesgo relativo
p[p > 0.95] <- 0.95  # evitar probabilidades mayores a 1

rechazado <- rbinom(n, size = 1, prob = p)

# Dataset final
datos <- data.frame(rechazado, producto, proveedor, temperatura)
head(datos, 10)

Modelo Poisson con Varianza Robusta

# ---- Modelo Poisson con varianza robusta ----
modelo <- glm(rechazado ~ producto + proveedor + temperatura,
              family = poisson(link = "log"), data = datos)

check_model(modelo)

# Visualisar resultados del modelo
fancy_plot = ggeffect(modelo) |> plot() |> plot_grid()

extract_eq(modelo, wrap = TRUE, intercept = 'beta',
           show_distribution = TRUE)
## This distribution is not presently supported; the distribution assumption
##       will not be displayed

\[ \begin{aligned} \log ({ E( \operatorname{rechazado} ) }) &= \beta_{0} + \beta_{1}(\operatorname{producto}_{\operatorname{Lácteo}}) + \beta_{2}(\operatorname{producto}_{\operatorname{Vegetal}}) + \beta_{3}(\operatorname{proveedor}_{\operatorname{B}})\ + \\ &\quad \beta_{4}(\operatorname{temperatura}) \end{aligned} \]

extract_eq(modelo, wrap = TRUE, intercept = 'beta',
           use_coefs = T, show_distribution = TRUE)
## This distribution is not presently supported; the distribution assumption
##       will not be displayed

\[ \begin{aligned} \log ({ \widehat{E( \operatorname{rechazado} )} }) &= -0.02 - 0.02(\operatorname{producto}_{\operatorname{Lácteo}}) + 0.02(\operatorname{producto}_{\operatorname{Vegetal}}) + 0.01(\operatorname{proveedor}_{\operatorname{B}})\ + \\ &\quad 0(\operatorname{temperatura}) \end{aligned} \]

emmeans(modelo, pairwise ~ producto,
        type = 'response', infer = T)
## $emmeans
##  producto  rate     SE  df asymp.LCL asymp.UCL null z.ratio p.value
##  Cárnico  0.961 0.0541 Inf     0.861      1.07    1  -0.703  0.4821
##  Lácteo   0.939 0.0537 Inf     0.839      1.05    1  -1.106  0.2689
##  Vegetal  0.979 0.0535 Inf     0.880      1.09    1  -0.383  0.7017
## 
## Results are averaged over the levels of: proveedor 
## Confidence level used: 0.95 
## Intervals are back-transformed from the log scale 
## Tests are performed on the log scale 
## 
## $contrasts
##  contrast          ratio     SE  df asymp.LCL asymp.UCL null z.ratio p.value
##  Cárnico / Lácteo  1.024 0.0821 Inf     0.849      1.24    1   0.295  0.9531
##  Cárnico / Vegetal 0.982 0.0771 Inf     0.817      1.18    1  -0.237  0.9695
##  Lácteo / Vegetal  0.959 0.0758 Inf     0.796      1.15    1  -0.535  0.8541
## 
## Results are averaged over the levels of: proveedor 
## Confidence level used: 0.95 
## Conf-level adjustment: tukey method for comparing a family of 3 estimates 
## Intervals are back-transformed from the log scale 
## P value adjustment: tukey method for comparing a family of 3 estimates 
## Tests are performed on the log scale
emmeans(modelo, ~ producto, type = 'response') %>%
  pairs(reverse = T, infer = T)
##  contrast          ratio     SE  df asymp.LCL asymp.UCL null z.ratio p.value
##  Lácteo / Cárnico  0.977 0.0783 Inf     0.809      1.18    1  -0.295  0.9531
##  Vegetal / Cárnico 1.019 0.0800 Inf     0.848      1.22    1   0.237  0.9695
##  Vegetal / Lácteo  1.043 0.0825 Inf     0.867      1.26    1   0.535  0.8541
## 
## Results are averaged over the levels of: proveedor 
## Confidence level used: 0.95 
## Conf-level adjustment: tukey method for comparing a family of 3 estimates 
## Intervals are back-transformed from the log scale 
## P value adjustment: tukey method for comparing a family of 3 estimates 
## Tests are performed on the log scale
nice_table = tbl_regression(modelo,
                            exponentiate = TRUE,
                            add_pairwise_contrasts = TRUE,
                            weights= 'prop',
                            pairwise_reverse = FALSE) |>
  
  # pimp your table
  add_significance_stars(hide_p = FALSE, hide_se = TRUE, hide_ci = FALSE) |>
  modify_header(label = '**Predictor**') |>
  modify_caption('Table 1. Nice looking table!') |>
  modify_footnote(abbreviation = TRUE) |>
  bold_labels() |>
  italicize_levels() |>
  bold_p()

REGRESIÓN LOG BINOMIAL (Usando la librería MASS)

modelo_logbin = logbin(rechazado ~ producto + proveedor + temperatura,
                       data = datos)

check_model(modelo_logbin)

fancy_plot1 = ggeffect(modelo_logbin) |> plot() |> plot_grid()

extract_eq(modelo_logbin, wrap = TRUE, intercept = 'beta',
           show_distribution = TRUE)

\[ \begin{aligned} \operatorname{rechazado} &\sim Bernoulli\left(\operatorname{prob}_{\operatorname{rechazado} = \operatorname{1}}= \hat{P}\right) \\ \log ({ \hat{P} }) &= \beta_{0} + \beta_{1}(\operatorname{producto}_{\operatorname{Lácteo}}) + \beta_{2}(\operatorname{producto}_{\operatorname{Vegetal}}) + \beta_{3}(\operatorname{proveedor}_{\operatorname{B}})\ + \\ &\quad \beta_{4}(\operatorname{temperatura}) \end{aligned} \]

extract_eq(modelo_logbin, wrap = TRUE, intercept = 'beta',
           use_coefs = T, show_distribution = TRUE)

\[ \begin{aligned} \operatorname{rechazado} &\sim Bernoulli\left(\operatorname{prob}_{\operatorname{rechazado} = \operatorname{1}}= \hat{P}\right) \\ \log ({ \hat{P} }) &= 0.01 - 0.03(\operatorname{producto}_{\operatorname{Lácteo}}) + 0.02(\operatorname{producto}_{\operatorname{Vegetal}}) + 0(\operatorname{proveedor}_{\operatorname{B}})\ + \\ &\quad 0(\operatorname{temperatura}) \end{aligned} \]

emmeans(modelo_logbin, pairwise ~ producto,
        type = 'response', infer = T)
## $emmeans
##  producto  prob     SE  df asymp.LCL asymp.UCL null z.ratio p.value
##  Cárnico  0.962 0.0105 Inf     0.941     0.983    1  -3.559  0.0004
##  Lácteo   0.938 0.0134 Inf     0.912     0.964    1  -4.514  <.0001
##  Vegetal  0.980 0.0076 Inf     0.965     0.995    1  -2.667  0.0077
## 
## Results are averaged over the levels of: proveedor 
## Confidence level used: 0.95 
## Intervals are back-transformed from the log scale 
## Tests are performed on the log scale 
## 
## $contrasts
##  contrast          ratio     SE  df asymp.LCL asymp.UCL null z.ratio p.value
##  Cárnico / Lácteo  1.026 0.0184 Inf     0.984     1.070    1   1.421  0.3302
##  Cárnico / Vegetal 0.982 0.0131 Inf     0.952     1.013    1  -1.363  0.3606
##  Lácteo / Vegetal  0.957 0.0155 Inf     0.921     0.994    1  -2.695  0.0193
## 
## Results are averaged over the levels of: proveedor 
## Confidence level used: 0.95 
## Conf-level adjustment: tukey method for comparing a family of 3 estimates 
## Intervals are back-transformed from the log scale 
## P value adjustment: tukey method for comparing a family of 3 estimates 
## Tests are performed on the log scale
emmeans(modelo_logbin, ~ producto, type = 'response') %>%
  pairs(reverse = T, infer = T)
##  contrast          ratio     SE  df asymp.LCL asymp.UCL null z.ratio p.value
##  Lácteo / Cárnico  0.975 0.0175 Inf     0.935      1.02    1  -1.421  0.3302

nice_table = tbl_regression(modelo_logbin,
